Frequently Asked

Buying property in the UK from India — the real questions.

Can resident Indians legally buy property in the UK?

Yes. Resident Indians can buy property abroad using the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), which permits remittances of up to USD 250,000 per person per financial year for permitted purposes, including the purchase of property overseas.

How much can I remit for a London property under LRS?

Up to USD 250,000 per financial year (April–March) per individual. The limit is per person, not per purchase — co-investing with a spouse or family member can combine limits, provided the property is held jointly.

What is TCS, and how much will I pay on my remittance?

Tax Collected at Source (TCS) is an advance tax collected on LRS remittances. Under current rules, it's nil on the first ₹10 lakh remitted in a financial year and 20% on the remainder for property purchases — and it can be claimed back as a credit against your income tax liability. Rates are set by the Government of India and can change; we walk through the exact numbers for your situation on the discovery call and in the free roadmap.

Do I need to travel to London to complete the purchase?

No. Site visits and virtual walkthroughs are both available, and your solicitor handles legal completion remotely. Many of our clients complete their purchase without visiting the UK in person.

Are the rental yields you quote guaranteed?

No. Any yield figures shown are developer or agent estimates based on current market conditions, not guarantees. Actual rental income depends on the property being let continuously at the estimated rent, among other factors.

What happens after I submit an enquiry?

You'll receive the free LRS & TCS roadmap, then move through our three-step process: a fit & funding call with our Mumbai team, a virtual walkthrough of your shortlisted property, and a solicitor-coordinated closing.
